r03_00.why: A dark centred void with a hard material boundary at mid-height, so it tiles into a grid of holes over horizontal stripes; no fixings, no timber, no top band, and column 31 does not continue into column 0.

r03_01.why: A black doorway rectangle standing on a pale floor strip — that is a scene containing a wall, not a piece of wall, and the brick field behind it is one stamp repeated with nothing holding it together.

r03_02.why: A candle prop and scattered debris sitting on a green ground band, with the upper two thirds collapsing into undifferentiated dark checker that has no courses, joints or fixings.

r03_03.why: A lit brazier — dark mass, flame, plinth, floor line — placed centred on a brick backdrop; repeating it produces a rank of braziers, not a wall.

r03_04.why: Flat horizontal stripes with a stencilled hook motif in saturated mint — reads as woven awning or wallpaper, has zero thickness, no front face, no top surface, and nothing has happened to it.

r03_05.why: A mirror-symmetric hearth mouth with checkered flanking panels and a green mass spilling from it — a discrete centred feature, and the bottom half is ground plane rather than wall.

r03_06.why: One brick stamp repeated mechanically with no variation, capped by a black band and a bright line that stripe the whole map and repeat their rust flecks pixel-for-pixel every 32px; nothing structural holds it together and nothing has been done to it.

r03_07.why: A framed archway with a lighter surround and a rubble mound at its foot — an architectural feature that must be its own tile, not repeatable surface.

r03_08.why: An arbitrary crop of a scene — a light column welded to the right edge, a floating T-bracket, a green ground band — which tiles into a grid of framed dark panels with a hard seam down every column boundary.

r03_09.why: A rectangular checkered slab floating on flat teal with margin on all four sides and a little hatch prop stuck to its base — a sprite, not a surface.

flip_list: Delete every centred feature — the doorway in r03_01, the brazier in r03_03, the hearth mouth in r03_05, the arch in r03_07, the hatch in r03_09 — from the wall candidates. A wall tile carries no unique landmark; landmarks are separate tiles.
Remove the ground band along the bottom of r03_00, r03_01, r03_02, r03_04, r03_05, r03_07 and r03_08. Wall must run to row 31; the floor is a different tile.

Move the depth cue to the top edge: rows 0–4 are the wall's top surface, one flat value step off the front face and a different hue, and rows 5–31 are the front face. Do this on r03_06 and r03_08, which are the only two with a usable masonry field.

Make the tile wrap. Column 31 must continue the same course into column 0, and row 31 into row 0. Currently r03_00, r03_02, r03_04, r03_06 and r03_08 break hardest across the horizontal seam and r03_08 across the vertical one — redraw the outer two pixels of each edge so no joint, block or band terminates at the border.
On r03_09, bleed the masonry out to all four edges and delete the flat teal field entirely; there is no background in a wall tile.

Break r03_06's single brick stamp: make the courses uneven in height, offset the vertical joints irregularly, and replace three or four blocks with cracked or mismatched salvage so no 8px region repeats.

Add the repair hardware the fiction requires and none of these have: a salvaged timber baulk laid horizontally across the full tile width, running off both edges so it continues into the neighbouring tile, with a driven iron pin at two points — each pin a 2x2 head with a bitten-in rim, not a dot — and one rope lashing wrapped over the timber where it crosses a joint.

Where masonry has been repaired, show the pattern of it: pack the gap around a replaced block with smaller chipped stone and a coarser mortar of a different value, so the eye can read old block / new packing / old block.

Drop the saturated mint and spring green in r03_04, r03_05, r03_07 and r03_08 by roughly half their chroma and pull them toward grey-olive; keep green only as a thin residue in the joints, never as a field colour.
Rebuild r03_04 from scratch as masonry. Horizontal stripes of alternating hue with a stencilled motif cannot be made to read as stone by editing; it needs courses, joints and a front face.
